mainTopic: Whether eating food with שלישי טומאה makes a person impure for תרומה and קודש: the rulings of עולא, רבי יונתן and רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא, רמי בר חמא's challenge, and the proof from מדרס.
overview: This amud opens with the last words of an earlier explanation: a mixture does not need the purity of תרומה, because the eater never takes in a כזית of the תרומה within כדי אכילת פרס. Then רבי יונתן quotes רבי: someone who eats actual תרומה that is a שלישי may not eat תרומה, but may still touch it. The גמרא explains why this ruling and the earlier ruling of עולא are both needed. Next, רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא rules that eating a שלישי of חולין prepared with the purity of קודש does not stop a person from eating קודש, because only real קודש creates a רביעי. רמי בר חמא challenges him from a משנה. That משנה says eating a שלישי makes a person a שני for קודש, even though its case must be about חולין prepared like תרומה. רב יצחק answers that the purity of תרומה already counts as impurity when it comes to קודש. The גמרא supports this from the משנה about clothing, where each group's clothing is מדרס for the group above it. רבא starts to reject that proof by saying מדרס is a special case, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing reason: not a כזית within the time of כדי אכילת פרס
steps.stepSummary: The last words of an earlier explanation. The amount of תרומה a person eats in the set time is less than a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there is not an olive-sized amount of it within the time it takes to eat half a loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an explanation from the previous page. The mixture has no special purity rules because the eater never takes in a כזית of the תרומה within כדי אכילת פרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating only counts as eating in הלכה if a כזית is eaten within a set amount of time, called כדי אכילת פרס. When the תרומה is spread thin through a larger dish, you never reach a כזית of it in that time. So the dish does not need to be guarded with the purity of תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-sized amount, the smallest amount that counts as 'eating' in halacha
The time it takes to eat half a loaf. A כזית must be eaten within this time to count as one act of eating

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of a discussion that began before this section. It is not the start of a new topic.

phrases.english: As there is not an olive-bulk
phrases.notes: He means there is not a כזית of the תרומה in the mixture.

phrases.english: within the time of eating a half-loaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning that began on the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Less than a כזית within כדי אכילת פרס does not count as eating, so the mixture does not need תרומה-level purity.

steps.title: Eating a שלישי of real תרומה: no eating תרומה, but touching is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן quotes רבי. A person who eats תרומה that is a שלישי may not eat תרומה afterward, but he may touch it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן said in the name of רבי: Someone who eats real תרומה that is impure at the third level may not eat תרומה, but he is allowed to touch it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling is brought about a person who ate תרומה that is a שלישי. He becomes unfit to eat תרומה, but not unfit to touch it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating impure food makes a person's body impure, but only in a limited way. Here that limited impurity is enough to stop him from eating תרומה. It is not enough to make the תרומה impure just by touching it.

keyTerms.meaning: Third-degree טומאה. It can only make תרומה or קודש impure, not plain food
Actual תרומה, as opposed to plain food handled with the purity of תרומה
Forbidden to eat, but permitted to touch

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan said that Rabbi said:
One who eats a third-degree item of actual teruma –
is forbidden to eat, but permitted to touch.
phrases.notes: He means he may not eat תרומה, but he may touch תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ruling to עולא's earlier ruling, this time about actual תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating a שלישי of real תרומה stops a person from eating תרומה, but he may still touch it.

steps.title: Why we need both עולא and רבי יונתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that each ruling teaches something the other could not. If we only had one of them, we could have drawn the wrong conclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both rulings are needed. If we only had עולא, I would think his rule is only for חולין prepared with תרומה purity, and that real תרומה forbids even touching. So רבי יונתן was needed. If we only had רבי יונתן, I would think his rule is only for real תרומה, and that eating such חולין is fully permitted. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why say the same idea twice? It shows what mistake we might have made with only one of the two rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real תרומה is more serious than חולין handled with תרומה purity. From עולא alone, we might think real תרומה is even stricter and forbids touching too. רבי יונתן teaches that it does not. From רבי יונתן alone, we might think the weaker case of חולין is fully lenient, even for eating תרומה. עולא teaches that eating is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary / they are both necessary. This is how the גמרא shows that two rulings are not repeating each other
I would have thought. This introduces a mistaken first guess
Plain food that was handled with the same care as תרומה
This applies only to... It limits a rule to one case

steps.whatToRemember: The two rulings together give one rule. Eating a שלישי, whether of real תרומה or of חולין kept with תרומה purity, forbids eating תרומה but allows touching it.

phrases.english: And Ulla's statement was necessary, and Rabbi Yonatan's was necessary,
for if from Ulla alone, I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּחוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: this applies to non-sacred food prepared with the purity of teruma,
but with teruma itself, touching is also forbidden,
so Rabbi Yonatan's statement was necessary.
And if from Rabbi Yonatan alone, I would have said:
this applies to teruma,
but with non-sacred food, eating is also permitted,
phrases.notes: He means eating תרומה afterward would be allowed too.

phrases.english: so both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי יונתן's ruling (step 2) and עולא's earlier ruling are both needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each ruling blocks a different mistaken first guess
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From עולא alone: real תרומה forbids touching too. From רבי יונתן alone: חולין prepared with תרומה purity allows even eating תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: In both cases, eating תרומה is forbidden and touching is allowed.

steps.title: Eating a שלישי of חולין prepared with קודש purity: may still eat קודש
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא rules in front of רב נחמן. Someone who ate a שלישי of חולין prepared with the purity of קודש may still eat קודש, because only real קודש can create a רביעי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא sat before רב נחמן and said: Someone who eats third-degree חולין that was prepared with the purity of קודש is pure to eat קודש. The reason is that nothing creates a fourth level of impurity in קודש except real קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling begins, now about קודש. Eating such חולין does not make the person unfit to eat קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קודש, a שלישי can usually pass impurity on and make a רביעי. This ruling says only real קודש has that power. חולין handled with קודש-level care stops at שלישי, so it cannot affect the person or the קודש he eats.

keyTerms.meaning: The purity level required for קודש (sacrificial food)
Fourth-degree טומאה, which only exists in קודש
Only real קודש can produce impurity in קודש at that level

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a limit: the strict level of רביעי belongs only to real קודש, not to חולין that is just treated like קודש.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta was sitting
before Rav Nachman, and he sat and said:
One who eats a third-degree item of non-sacred food
that was prepared with the purity of sacred food –
is pure to eat sacred food,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה רְבִיעִי בַּקֹּדֶשׁ
phrases.english: for there is nothing that creates a fourth degree in sacred food
except actual sacred food alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rules for תרומה to a parallel question about קודש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating a שלישי of חולין prepared with קודש purity does not make a person unfit to eat קודש, because only real קודש creates a רביעי.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא challenges from a case of חולין prepared like תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא quotes a משנה. Someone who eats a שלישי becomes a שני for קודש. That case can only be about חולין prepared with the purity of תרומה, which is not קודש. So how can it make him impure for קודש?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא objects: The משנה says a person who eats a שלישי becomes a שני for קודש but not for תרומה. This must be about חולין that were prepared with the purity of תרומה. Why should that make him a שני for קודש? It is not real קודש!
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא attacks the ruling from step 4, that only real קודש can make someone impure for קודש. He points to a משנה where food that is not קודש still makes a person a שני for קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said that eating a שלישי of חולין does not affect a person for קודש unless the food is real קודש. But the משנה's case cannot be about real קודש or real תרומה, because impure תרומה may not be eaten. So it must be חולין prepared like תרומה, and the משנה still says the person becomes a שני for קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Second level of impurity
The level of care in purity that is used for תרומה
Real, actually holy קודש (not just food prepared with that care)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה is talking about real תרומה. A person may not eat impure תרומה, so the case has to be about חולין that were prepared with the purity of תרומה.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama raises an objection:
[One who eats] a third becomes a second for קודש,
and not a second for תרומה.
[This is] about חולין that were made with the purity of תרומה.
Why?
It is not real קודש!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only real קודש can make a person impure for קודש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה, food that is not real קודש (חולין prepared like תרומה) still makes the eater a שני for קודש.

steps.title: The purity of תרומה counts as impurity for קודש
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא answers that the case of תרומה is different. Food prepared only with the purity of תרומה is treated as impure when it comes to קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Leave תרומה aside. Its purity counts as impurity compared to קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא defends his ruling. He explains that food kept at the purity level of תרומה is already considered impure as far as קודש goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His rule in step 4 was about חולין prepared with the purity of קודש. Food prepared only with the purity of תרומה starts out as not pure enough for קודש. That is why it can make a person a שני for קודש even though it is not real קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave תרומה aside; it is a different case
Counted as impurity when compared to קודש

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea of levels of purity: something can be pure for one level of holiness and impure for a higher one.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: The one answering is רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא, from step 4.

phrases.english: Leave תרומה aside,
because its purity is impurity compared to קודש.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the purity of תרומה versus the purity of קודש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only real קודש can make someone impure for קודש, so חולין prepared like תרומה should not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Food prepared with the purity of תרומה is already considered impure for קודש, so it can make a person a שני for קודש.

steps.title: A source from the clothing of different groups
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we know that the purity of תרומה is impurity for קודש. It quotes a משנה: each group's clothing counts as מדרס for the group above it, and the clothing of those who eat תרומה counts as מדרס for קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you say this? As we learned: The clothing of an עם הארץ is מדרס for פרושים. The clothing of פרושים is מדרס for those who eat תרומה. The clothing of those who eat תרומה is מדרס for קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the idea in step 6 and brings a משנה as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists a ladder of purity levels. Even clothing kept at the purity level of תרומה is treated as impure, like מדרס, for someone dealing with קודש. This seems to prove that the purity of תרומה is impurity compared to קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (a request for a source)
Someone who is not careful about purity laws
Impurity of something a זב or נדה leaned or sat on; a primary source of impurity
People who carefully eat even their חולין in purity

phrases.english: And from where do you say this?
As we learned [in a משנה]:
The clothing of an עם הארץ
is מדרס for פרושים,
phrases.notes: For them it is treated like a main source of impurity.

phrases.english: the clothing of פרושים is מדרס for those who eat תרומה,
the clothing of those who eat תרומה is מדרס for קודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the answer in step 6
steps.raayaObject: The purity of תרומה counts as impurity for קודש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that lists the clothing of each group as מדרס for the group above it

steps.title: רבא says מדרס is a special case
steps.stepSummary: רבא questions the proof. He says the laws of מדרס are different, so we cannot learn a general rule from them. His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You are bringing a proof from מדרס? מדרס is different,
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins to reject the proof from the משנה about clothing. This line sets up his explanation of why מדרס is different, which continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 7 assumed that the מדרס ladder shows a general rule about purity levels. רבא says it is a special rule about clothing and מדרס. So it may not prove that food prepared with the purity of תרומה is impure for קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different (used to say a source is a special case)
Cases of מדרס impurity

phrases.english: Rava said:
You are speaking about מדרס?
מדרס is different,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִדְרָסוֹת קָאָמְרַתְּ? שָׁאנֵי מִדְרָסוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the מדרס משנה, not necessarily the rule itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מדרס may be a special case, so a general rule about the purity of תרומה cannot be learned from it.
